scope: Native Win32 volume-namespace enumeration and explicitly selected mount-path observations. This is one component of native inventory, not physical disk identity, full topology, a public command or admitted provider.
api_reference_floor: Microsoft documents these volume enumeration/mount APIs for XP desktop applications. Selected modern compiler/CRT/import closure and actual XP launch remain separately unqualified.
execution: Construction performs no query. Only explicit collect dispatches enumeration. No application file/device opens, labels, filesystem/capacity reads, raw access, IOCTL, application media reads, deep tests, elevation, network, writes or installer/service actions. Default product startup remains unchanged. Qualification injects exact Win32 API replies; no host namespace is enumerated. Metadata API implementations may themselves access storage; no idle-media/no-spin-up or preservation claim follows.
names: Preserve exact original UTF-16 code units as lowercase little-endian byte hex, separate from ASCII display with every nonprinting/non-ASCII unit escaped as \uXXXX. Do not normalize, replace invalid surrogate units or execute text. Volume names must have the documented ASCII volume-GUID syntax before mount query. Mounts remain presentation paths, never storage identity or access authority. Even exact/ASCII-case duplicate paths are only observed conflicts; no complete filesystem-alias proof is claimed.
identity: Each record has a capture/ordinal observation ID, not a disk ordinal or physical-media ID. Retain duplicate volume names and conflicting mount aliases as separate observations. Volume names, serials, GUIDs and path spelling do not authorize mutation; physical identity/capacity/layout/backing layers remain unknown. No cross-capture identity merge.
api_parsing: Bound every native output buffer. FindFirst/Next success requires a NUL within the fixed 64-unit name buffer. Native last error is captured immediately. Only ERROR_NO_MORE_FILES establishes enumeration exhaustion; denial/removal/failure is explicit. Mount MULTI_SZ uses the API's returned unit count, validates exact termination, each path/count and all budgets. Accept an empty one- or two-NUL list. ERROR_MORE_DATA may trigger one bounded growth when the required count is larger and within remaining budget; inconsistent count or repeated growth refuses the observation. Never publish partial buffer contents as a complete list.
budgets: Positive capture epoch is u64. Selected limits cannot exceed fixed maxima. Check cancellation before first/next/mount dispatch. Stop before exceeding accepted volume or total mount budgets and retain prior records with explicit partial/unknown remainder. Snapshot bytes/values/depth/string budgets apply to the complete view, without truncation. API latency itself is not universally bounded by these count/byte rules; containment and product waits remain future admission gates.
close: Close a started search once, including cancellation, malformed input and exceptions. A failed close remains uncertain and is never retried by destruction or reinterpreted as quiescence. Reusing a cursor cannot restart enumeration. Observation completion and actual enclosing-process exit remain separate.
required_checks: No API call on construction/help/invalid input; exact native table and callback arguments; enumeration handle closes once.
Empty exhausted inventory differs from denied/unavailable/removal; terminal error preserves prior entries.
Duplicate GUID spellings, alias conflicts and reordered entries never merge physical identities or select a destructive target.
Missing NUL, oversized/inconsistent MULTI_SZ, repeated ERROR_MORE_DATA, exact budgets and cancellation stop before further queries; prior accepted observations remain visible.
Exact UTF-16 byte preservation and inert display for Unicode, control, bidi and unpaired surrogate units.
Close failure/exception/reuse retains uncertainty without retry; actual fixture process exit is observed separately.
Compile and execute exact source under selected modern x64 and x86 toolchains, retain imports and distinguish API documentation floor from real XP support.
